articles.title: Karnataka likely to receive widespread rain till September 24: IMD - Deccan Herald

Bengaluru: The India Meteorological Departmen (IMD) has forecast a significant increase in rainfall activity across Karnataka from Saturday, with a yellow alert in place for several districts until September 24 as a weather system in the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify.

Forecast for the next six days

IMD scientist C S Patil said that while only isolated light rain was recorded on September 18, the situation is set to change over the next week. From September 19 to 24, most parts of north interior Karnataka, south interior Karnataka and the coastal districts are likely to experience light to moderate, fairly widespread to widespread rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning.

.Mysuru weather: Sudden rains in city bring respite from scorching heat.

In several districts: Uttara Kannada, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Belagavi, Dharwad, Haveri, Gadag, Bidar, Kalaburagi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Hassan, Kodagu and Bengaluru (urban and rural) heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places.

A yellow alert has been issued for these districts for the six-day period, warning residents and authorities to remain vigilant.

Bengaluru outlook

For Bengaluru specifically, the IMD predicts: Light to moderate rain over the next five days, with thunder and lightning likely at times. Gusty winds of 30–40 kmph may accompany some of the showers. Temperatures are expected to remain in the low 20s (minimum) to around 30–31°C (maximum) during this period.

Patil noted that Karnataka is currently grappling with a rainfall deficit of about 26–27% for the season, leaving farmers anxious about crop prospects and water availability. While the deficit may not be fully erased, the expected widespread showers should help recharge soils and reservoirs to some extent across south interior and coastal regions as well.

Drought situation arises in Maharashtra districts as CM Fadnavis announces relief measures
Devendra Fadnavis said Maharashtra faces a drought-like situation after a prolonged break in rain damaged standing crops. The state will begin assessments, crop surveys and relief measures as farmers confront water, fodder and power stress.
Advertisement
Fadnavis said three lists had already been issued as part of the loan waiver process. (File Photo: ITG)
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday said a drought-like situation has developed in several districts of the state after a break in rains damaged standing crops. He said the issue was discussed in detail at a cabinet meeting, and ministers had been asked to carry out a preliminary assessment in their respective districts and make preparedness arrangements.
Fadnavis said the state government would complete its preliminary review within a week, after which official crop surveys, or panchnamas, would be conducted and immediate assistance provided.
He also said work on the farm loan waiver was under way, and that drinking water, fodder and additional evening power supply were being arranged for farmers.
Speaking to reporters, the chief minister said, "In the cabinet meeting, ministers discussed this carefully. I have instructed them to carry out preliminary assessment in their districts and make preparedness arrangements. I think within the next week we will complete preliminary review. After that we will conduct official crop surveys (panchnamas) and provide immediate assistance."
He said three lists had already been issued as part of the loan waiver process. "I have ordered that the remaining lists be complete quickly. Urgent assistance that farmers need will be provided by the government. Drinking water and fodder arrangements will be made," he said.
Referring to preparations for a possible weather-linked crisis, Fadnavis said, knowing that a crisis triggered by El Nino was likely, the state government had launched the 'Vairan' development programme to address fodder shortage.
"We have also arranged for farmers to receive additional electricity in the evenings. We are now supplying extra power across regions," he added, while expressing confidence that the measures being implemented by his government would provide relief to farmers.
According to the India Meteorological Department, the southwest monsoon covered the entire country on July 9 after setting in over Kerala on June 4. IMD data showed India recorded a rainfall deficit of 15 per cent between June 4 and September 19, with the Southern Peninsula the worst-affected region at 29 per cent deficit.
Maharashtra is part of this peninsula, and the state government has said it is reviewing the situation and preparing relief measures.
